predecessors.note: The PRRI was proclaimed on 15 February 1958 (infobox 17 February) inside the Republic of Indonesia; the Permesta rebels, founded 2 March 1957, 'pledged allegiance' on 17 February 1958.

successors.note: Infobox: disestablished 28 September 1961, 'succeeded by Guided democracy government'; the land returns to the Republic. The Permesta page: the last remnants 'surrendered and were given amnesty in 1961'; Kumontoy, the last commander, in early 1962.

The page does not locate Kotto Tingi and no page opened does (the Koto Tinggi page did not load), so Bukittinggi's coordinates stand in as a placeholder. Permesta's own headquarters (a second seat, not drawn here): Makassar to 20 June 1957, Manado to 24 June 1958 (124.85 E, 1.48 N), Tomohon to 16 August 1958 (124.839 E, 1.325 N), Kotamobagu to 14 September 1959 (124.317 E, 0.733 N).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The PRRI page lists Tapanuli (Pusuk Buhit Division), West Sumatra, Riau, Jambi and South Sumatra Regions; North Sulawesi is Permesta's (Dewan Manguni, 20 December 1956). The same union as the republic-of-indonesia dossier's contest zone. The page gives no extent of land held, so the whole named provinces are drawn for the founding year; the year's losses (Padang, Bukittinggi, Manado, Tomohon) are in the ledger. [Reviewer se-04-x: the same page also lists Barlian's Garuda Council (South Sumatra) among the unwilling parties, and its infobox puts only 'Central Sumatra province' under PRRI control in February 1958, so South Sumatra's inclusion is doubtful.]

ledger.note: 1958: the PRRI is proclaimed on 15 February by Lt Col Ahmad Hussein after a five-day ultimatum ('proclaimed to have been established on 15 February 1958'; infobox 17 February). Permesta 'had pledged allegiance with the PRRI on 17 February 1958'. The page does not say where it was proclaimed; Padang is the infobox's first capital, so Padang is where the capital dot starts.

ledger.note: 1958: the revolt against the Jakarta government begins over the named regions of Sumatra and North Sulawesi; the government 'arrested ministers, discharged commanders who supported the PRRI, and bombed key infrastructure in Sumatra' (no dates on the page).

wars.outcome: The central government retook Padang, Bukittinggi and Manado in 1958 and the PRRI ended on 28 September 1961 with amnesties; Permesta's last commander surrendered in early 1962.
wars.note: The page names no operations; dates are the infobox's capital changes and the Permesta page's headquarters and surrender dates. The earlier councils (Dewan Gajah took East Sumatra from 22 December 1956; Dewan Manguni took North Sulawesi on 20 December 1956) are precursors, not drawn.

certainty.note: A rebel government with no recorded boundary; the provinces are the pages' named regions and the cities are the only dated ground.

notes: Rebel state added by se-04-x; the counterpart slug and the zone repeat the republic-of-indonesia dossier's 1958-02 and 1961-09 contest events so the two pair. One dossier for the PRRI (Sumatra) and Permesta (Sulawesi), which allied on 17 February 1958 and ended in the same amnesty year; the PRRI page lists only the Sumatran regions, so North Sulawesi rests on the Permesta page. Permesta's battle-area commands (KDP I North Maluku, KDP II Minahasa, KDP III Bolmong-Gorontalo, KDP IV Central Sulawesi: Palu, Donggala, Toli-toli, Poso) reach beyond Sulawesi Utara; they are not drawn because the page does not say they were held (Gorontalo, Sulawesi Tengah and Maluku Utara are in the gazetteer if a gap-filler wants them). Dates disagree between pages: PRRI proclaimed 15 February (body) or 17 February (infobox); Permesta founded 2 March 1957 on its page but 'between March 1956 and October 1961' on the Tomohon page; Kumontoy's surrender early 1962 against the amnesty 1961. Not on the pages: the government's operations (Operation 17 August, Tegas, Merdeka), Pekanbaru, the place of proclamation, Kotto Tingi's position. The Koto Tinggi and Operation 17 August pages did not load. Gazetteer names wanted: Tomohon, Kotamobagu (places; currently radii), Koto Tinggi (place, West Sumatra).
